$comment: The only file in the pipeline that knows this repo's shape. Fill it in with docs/agents/review-onboarding.md open: every entry needs evidence from the repo, not a guess. Validate with `node .github/scripts/review-doctor.js`.
$comment.trigger: The pull request comment that starts a CI review. Must match the workflow - the doctor checks it.
$comment.coverageNotes: Metrics this run knows it cannot gather. Printed in the review as missing, rather than replaced by an ad-hoc analysis. Delete the entries that do not apply.

coverageNotes.Corpus: aidd_docs/memory is descriptive background; the anchored rules under docs/agents/rules are what a reviewer cites
coverageNotes.Coverage report: vitest coverage is not collected in CI, so no per-diff coverage delta is available

$comment.exclude: Files no reviewer may see: generated output, vendored code, lockfiles, snapshots, binaries. Each one is recorded with its reason in the review's coverage section. Add every generator output you found in the survey.

exclude.reason: vendored review-kit runtime — owned upstream, updated by re-running the installer
vendored subject profiles (MIT) — the input contract, not this repo's code

$comment.axes: One entry per reviewer. `always` runs every time; `route` is a regex over the changed paths and should over-select on purpose. `prefix` mints finding ids and must never be renamed. `web: true` grants WebFetch/WebSearch. `routeIncludesExcluded: true` also routes on excluded paths.

corpus.$comment.rules: Two consumers, one corpus. `docs/agents/{hexagon,criterion-contract}.md` are hand-written and anchored: one rule per heading with a permanent {#anchor}, cited as `<file>.md#<anchor>`, owned by axis in review-ownership.json. They sit flat in docsRoot (doc-lint scans it non-recursively); the process docs are excluded so only real rules enter the corpus. The `claude` surface is kept for rules AIDD may generate under .claude/rules later.
corpus.$comment.memory: aidd_docs/memory/*.md is the durable project context - architecture, coding-assertions, testing, vcs. Descriptive, not normative: what a reviewer reads for background, never what it cites.
